questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to find a good university with classes that was not offered at my home university. Furthermore, I looked for a university town where there were good opportunities to meet new people and with good study facilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything was communicated well - absolutely nothing wrong with Erasmus and communication from them!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome centre where I got all the assistance I needed. I chose to live in Stockholm and organise that myself which went well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had an advantage since my partner is from Sweden and had "queue days" in the student housing company in Stockholm (SSSB) - so we found an apartment through them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was cool in the beginning to live in Stockholm, but the delayed trains and train schedule were tiresome in the end. Especially in the winter, it was not nice when it took 2 hours to get home and it was cold and dark. Furthermore, in regards to the social life, it is quite difficult to meet new people in Uppsala when you live further away. I rarely went out in Uppsala because it would mean I had to find somewhere to stay the night. With all that said, Stockholm is a much larger city than Uppsala and I'm still very glad I got to live here, as I am more of a big city person in general. I've heard others being tired of how small Uppsala is.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You applied through a link they sent via e-mail, and then you just chose the courses you would like. Luckily, I got the courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They sent reminders via e-mail, the website was very easy and helpful. If I had any issues, I just sent an e-mail to the Mobility-office, and would receive a reply very quick.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into classes that are not offered at your home university. I thought it was a nice opportunity to learn something which would normally not be accessible to me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one course with a teacher who would ignore our emails, take months to grade our (many) papers and never give any feedback (although that was a part of the course). Overall, I think the English department at Uppsala is a bit disorganised with a few teachers as exceptions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one BA-level course, which turned out to be the most difficult course. It was very interesting and I learned a lot, however, there was a much too large work load packed into this course (which was only a 7.5 ects point course) - this course was called 'Investigating the Structure of English then and now'. I had three other courses that were a part of the 'English Linguistics' Master's programme. I thought the work load and level of these were appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I would say it was a bit more disorganised than that of UCPH. Some teachers were really great and had planned their course great, however, the others were either ambiguous or had been teaching for way too many years to care about their course. I think Engerom at UCPH is much better at creating a fun environment with new and exciting teaching methods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
5EN445: From Project to Paper: Writing about Linguistic Research. 
5EN490: Language in Society: Theory, Analysis and Interpretation.
5EN491: Introduction to Corpus Linguistics.
5EN165: Investigating the Structure of English then and now: From 'elne mycle' to 'with great zeal'.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 'Language in Society' and 'Introduction to Corpus Linguistics' were great course with great teachers. Especially the Corpus Linguistics course was very interesting and I have learned a lot about that methodology which I will be using for my thesis.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I guess they were fine, but I did not use any of them except going to the Nations club a couple of times.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are the so-called 'Nations' which are sororities/fraternities (although not divided by gender) with a lot of activities for students. Their bars and clubs were fun to visit.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely join a nation. I was not there as much, but if I had lived in Uppsala (not Stockholm), I would have used the nations a lot more. They seem like good places to meet friends and party. They also have study cafés with student pricing.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stockholm is a must. I've heard it's nice up north as well. A lot of students went camping, which looked great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since Denmark and Sweden are so alike.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would say, join a nation and participate in all the activities. I met friends on the intro day. Also, the Goin' app is really great to find others with similar interests as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The local, Uppsala culture is very student-oriented (since it is a student town). The nations were cool to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Live in Uppsala if you want to make friends, 2. Join a nation, 3. Look into the difficulty of the course before you go according to how much time you want to spent on classes and exams.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was a bit disappointment that the department I had classes in was so small. If you want to meet a lot of people, maybe look into how big the departments are.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses that I would not have had in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely that I lived in Stockholm and was so far away from the other exchange students. Generally, I did not make that many friends because I was not able to go out every weekend in Uppsala. Furthermore, the classes I were in were really small.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
